challenges.name: stale-page-or-data-leak-evidence
challenges.title: Stale Page or Data Leak? Read the evidence
challenges.description: The morning after a release that cached the dashboard, learners see another learner's name, lessons and streak for about a minute. Six statements on one evidence pack - the support tickets (A), the response headers (B), the cached data function and route handler (C) and the timeline (D) - take you from reading the evidence to a hypothesis, past two wrong explanations, to the fix and its verification.

questions.question:
Evidence B - response headers, Tue 09:15:
$ curl -sI https://app.codedev.test/api/dashboard -H "cookie: session=<Lan's session>"
HTTP/2 200
cache-control: public, s-maxage=60
age: 37
x-cache: HIT
etag: "d-41-19-8f2a"

$ curl -sI https://app.codedev.test/api/dashboard -H "cookie: session=<Thu's session>"
HTTP/2 200
cache-control: public, s-maxage=60
age: 38
x-cache: HIT
etag: "d-41-19-8f2a"

$ curl -s https://app.codedev.test/api/me -H "cookie: session=<Lan's session>" -D -
cache-control: private, no-store
x-cache: MISS
{"id":"u_2041","name":"Lan"}

Statement: "Thu's request was answered from a copy the CDN had stored earlier, without reaching the Next.js server: the same etag as Lan's response, an age of 38 seconds and x-cache: HIT."
questions.explanation: True. x-cache: HIT (the header name is vendor-specific) says the CDN answered from its store, and age: 38 says the stored copy was fetched from the origin 38 seconds earlier. Two different session cookies received the byte-identical response (same etag). The /api/me call shows what an origin answer looks like (x-cache: MISS, private, no-store). Reading the headers first tells you which layer answered before you open any code; the common mistake is to start debugging the application while the request never reached it.

questions.question:
Evidence B - response headers, Tue 09:15:
$ curl -sI https://app.codedev.test/api/dashboard -H "cookie: session=<Lan's session>"
HTTP/2 200
cache-control: public, s-maxage=60
age: 37
x-cache: HIT
etag: "d-41-19-8f2a"

$ curl -sI https://app.codedev.test/api/dashboard -H "cookie: session=<Thu's session>"
HTTP/2 200
cache-control: public, s-maxage=60
age: 38
x-cache: HIT
etag: "d-41-19-8f2a"

$ curl -s https://app.codedev.test/api/me -H "cookie: session=<Lan's session>" -D -
cache-control: private, no-store
x-cache: MISS
{"id":"u_2041","name":"Lan"}

Statement: "Each of the two requests carried a different session cookie, so a shared cache that follows the HTTP caching rules keeps a separate copy per cookie: the CDN cannot be the layer that mixed the two learners."
questions.explanation: False. A shared cache keys a stored response by the request URL, plus the request headers the response names in Vary. Cookies are not part of the key unless the response says Vary: Cookie, and this one does not. The header public, s-maxage=60 explicitly tells shared caches they may store the response and reuse it for 60 seconds, for any request to /api/dashboard. So the CDN did exactly what it was told, and B shows it serving one stored copy to two cookies. The misconception is that a cache somehow "knows" a response is personal because the request was authenticated; it only knows what the URL, Vary and Cache-Control say.

True. db.dashboardFor(session.userId) depends on the user, but the user id is read inside the closure and is not part of the key "dashboard", so the first learner to fill the entry is served to every learner for 60 seconds. Independently, the public header lets the CDN store that response under the URL /api/dashboard, which is the same for everyone. Purging and bypassing the CDN removed only the second layer, which is why An still saw Minh's progress at 09:36. The hypothesis explains all of A to D, including the one-minute self-healing (both TTLs are 60). The common mistake is to stop at the first layer you find.

Evidence D - timeline:
Mon 17:40  deploy 2026.10.26-2 (PR #611, PR #612)
Mon 17:41  origin requests to /api/dashboard drop from ~1,900/min to ~30/min
Tue 08:55  instructor publishes an edit to "SQL Basics" (typo in a lesson title)
Tue 09:12  ticket #5120
Tue 09:20  ticket #5124
Tue 09:34  on-call purges /api/dashboard at the CDN and adds a CDN rule: BYPASS /api/dashboard
Tue 09:36  ticket #5131
Tue 09:40  auth log, 09:30-09:40: every /api/dashboard request authenticated as the user of its own session cookie; 0 session errors

Statement: "The top bar shows Lan while the dashboard shows Minh's progress, so the most likely cause is a session mix-up in auth: some of Lan's requests were authenticated as Minh."
questions.explanation: False. If Lan's session resolved to Minh, every endpoint would say Minh. B shows /api/me, which is never cached (private, no-store, x-cache: MISS), returning Lan for Lan's cookie, and the auth log in D shows every dashboard request authenticated as its own cookie's user with no session errors. The session is right; the data served for it comes from a cache whose key ignores the user. Comparing an uncached endpoint with the cached one, using the same cookie, separates the two. The misconception is to blame auth for anything that involves the wrong user.

Mon 17:41  origin requests to /api/dashboard drop from ~1,900/min to ~30/min
Tue 08:55  instructor publishes an edit to "SQL Basics" (typo in a lesson title)
Tue 09:12  ticket #5120

Tue 09:36  ticket #5131

Statement: "This is a stale page after the instructor's 08:55 edit: the dashboard shows data from before the edit, and calling revalidatePath(\"/dashboard\") after every lesson completion would fix it."
questions.explanation: False. Stale means the right learner's data, but old. A shows another learner's data (Minh's name, lessons and streak shown to Lan), which is a leak, not staleness. D also puts the start at Monday 17:40, before the 08:55 edit, and the edit changed a course title, not anyone's progress. Revalidating the dashboard path would only empty the shared entry so that the next learner refills it: the leak would rotate faster, not stop. The question to ask first is whose data it is; a shorter TTL or more revalidation never fixes a key that leaves out the user.

True. On the release code both modes fail: with the CDN in front, Minh gets Lan's stored response (public, same URL); with the CDN bypassed, the data cache returns Lan's entry under "dashboard". With the fix, the key contains the user, so the data cache keeps one entry per learner (the expensive query is still cached for 60 seconds), and private keeps every shared cache from storing the response, while the public course list is still shared. Testing both modes matters because each half-fix passes one of them. The purge is needed because entries stored under the old public header live until they expire.

challenges.name: stale-page-or-data-leak
challenges.title: Stale Page or Data Leak?
challenges.description:
Since Monday's release, learners on app.codedev.test open their dashboard and sometimes see another learner's name, lessons and streak; an anonymous visitor has seen a learner's dashboard too. After a minute or so it fixes itself. The release cached the expensive dashboard query on the server (getDashboard) and added a Cache-Control header to the /api/dashboard route handler so the CDN could absorb the morning peak. Purging and bypassing the CDN did not stop the leak.

Fix the data layer and the route handler so that every learner only ever gets their own dashboard, with the CDN in front and with it bypassed, while: the dashboard query stays cached on the server for 60 seconds, one entry per learner (a second request by the same learner within 60 seconds must not query the database); /api/dashboard is sent with Cache-Control "private, no-cache"; anonymous requests still get 401 with "private, no-store"; and the course list stays public, cached on the server and by the CDN with "public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300".

The file contains a fake clock in seconds, the database (it counts queries), the server data cache cached(key, ttlSeconds, load), and a CDN that keys entries by path and query only (the session cookie is not part of its key) and stores 200 responses for s-maxage seconds unless Cache-Control contains private or no-store. Do not change them or the test runner.

Input: { "bypassCdn"?: boolean, "requests": [{ "at": seconds, "user": "u_lan" | null, "path": "/api/..." }, ...] }. The runner prints, per request, the status, the body, the CDN result (HIT, MISS or BYPASS) and the Cache-Control header, then the number of database queries.
hints: There are two caches between a learner and the database. For each one, ask: what does it use as the key, and does that key contain everything that changes the dashboard? Then run the starter with the CDN bypassed: does the leak stop?

Look at the key passed to cached(...) in getDashboard and at the Cache-Control header the /api/dashboard branch of handle() returns. Compare both with what the course list does, and decide which parts of the course list's caching are right for per-user data and which are not.

A similar case on a different route: a notifications endpoint cached as cached("notifications", 30, () => db.notificationsFor(userId)) with "public, s-maxage=30". Keying it as `notifications:${userId}` keeps one server entry per user, and sending "private, no-cache" stops shared caches from storing it; the public announcements endpoint next to it keeps its shared key and its public header.
